The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 25.05.2024.

2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 25.05.2024 at about 07.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. AP-39-SV-5543 proceeding on Soukya Road, near Flipkart Company, Anugondanahalli Hobli, Bengaluru Rural, at that time a Tata Goods Carrier bearing Reg. No. TN-70-AJ-0081 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life without following any traffic rules, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner motorcycle.
Due to forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained several grievous injuries.

Immediately,
the petitioner was shifted to K.B.Sanjeevini Hospital for first aid, again he was shifted to Manipal Hospital later shifted to St. John's Hospital and admitted as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.20,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food,
nourishment and conveyance charges.

The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 33 years, the petitioner was working as Delivery Boy at Appollo Medical Home and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the Peddakotla Nagarjuna vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 27 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67414075/
2 said work.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, respondent No.2 remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.

The respondent No.1 in its written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, this respondent issued the policy to the offending vehicle and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further the respondent No.1 denied the involvement of the offending Goods Carrier vehicle in the alleged accident and the rider of motorcycle was riding without wearing head-gear and without holding valid and effective driving license to ride the motorcycle as on the date of accident.

It is submitted that, accident did not take place due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle as alleged, as such petition is to be dismissed against the respondent No.1 as the said offending vehicle did not caused the alleged accident.
Further this respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, framed the following issues are as under:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of the Tata Goods Carrier bearing Reg. No. TN-70-AJ-0081 on 25.05.2024 at about 07.00 p.m., on Soukya road, near Flipkart Company,
Anugondanahalli Hobli, Bengaluru Rural District and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?
5.

In order to prove the case of the petitioner, examined Medical Record Technician at St. Johns Medical College and Hospital as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.4, examined Dr.
Shailesh A. V. Rao as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.5 to P.8 and petitioner's wife examined herself as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.9 to P.25 and closed their side.

8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident is unable to speak properly, completely depend on other person and loss of memory and under care and custody represented by his wife and natural guardian as PW.3 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.

Ex.P.23 is the Notarized copy of Driving License, Ex.P.24 is the Discharge Summary and Ex.P.25 is the Medical bill.
10. The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving by the driver of Tata Goods Carrier bearing Reg. No. TN-70-AJ-0081.
Ex.P.9 to 16 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

The Ex.P.11 (spot panchanama),
clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information,
held investigation and filed the Ex.P.16, Charge-Sheet against the driver of offending vehicle U/s.
279 and 338 of IPC.
The Ex.
, certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles in question.
11. Learned counsel for petitioner contended that, the accident is caused due to rash and negligent act of driver of the offending vehicle.
Contesting respondent argued that, because of negligent act of petitioner himself accident has taken place.
Further he argued that, due to the impact of the accident petitioner not able to speak properly and he is completely depending upon others.

12. On the other hand, learned counsel for insurance company argued that, at the time of accident petitioner was not wearing head-guard and due to his negligence he sustained injuries in the accident and as such he argued that, petitioner also contributed his negligence to the cause of accident.

In support of his arguments he relied upon the following Judgments,
(i) 2009 (13) SCC 654 between Rajarani and others Vs. Oriental Insurance Co., wherein Hon'ble Apex Court observed that, contributory negligence does not mean breach of any duty.

sentences.text: It only means the failure by a person to use a reasonable care for the safety of either himself or his property.

D., KSRTC, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that, deceased was driving the motorcycle on a down gradient road Peddakotla Nagarjuna vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 27 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67414075/

sentences.text: Based upon the said finding Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considered the negligence on the part of deceased victim also.

13. It must be noted that, in the cross- examination of PW.3, it is suggested by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 that, the accident had happened because of the negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle, but witness denied the said suggestion.
No matter whether PW.3 admits the said suggestion or not, but in my opinion, the said suggestion is sufficient to conclude that, respondents have admitted the accident.
In other words, it is well settled that, suggestion is the reflection of the case of the opponent.

Therefore, in my view, by posing a suggestion to the effect that, the accident had occurred because of the negligence of the rider of motorcycle and the respondents have admitted that, the accident in question had happened.
14. The next question would be, on whose fault accident has occurred.

This question arises because in the written statement filed by respondent No.1, in which the respondent No.1 has raised the specific defence that, the accident had happened due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
Thus, the question would be whether this say of the respondent No.1 can be accepted or not.

It is true that, in the cross-examination of PW.3, learned counsel for respondent No.1 has posed question to the PW.3 that, accident is happened due to the negligence of petitioner himself, but PW.3 had denied the said suggestion.
However, it is important to note that, the second respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Further, the second respondent has not adduced any evidence before the Court.
Thus, these facts, make it clear that, except allegations, the respondent No.1 has not made any efforts to show that, accident had happened because of the fault of the rider of motorcycle.

15. The learned counsel for insurance company argued that, as per discharge summary at the time of accident petitioner was not wearing head-guard and during the cross-examination of PW.2 i.e.,
Doctor himself admits that, severity of brain injury might be less if petitioner wear the head-guard.
In support of his argument he also relied upon the above noted Judgments.
On perusal of the above decisions, in 2009 (13) SCC 654 the Truck was parked in the middle of the road i.e., it was stationary.
The claimant's car was being driven at nominal speed, oweing to another vehicle coming from the other side as the parking lights of the truck being not on, it was cited at the last minute.
Considering the said fact, Hon'ble Apex Court confirmed the order of Tribunal in respect of contributory negligence on the part of deceased also.

In another decision, 2021 ACJ 894 wherein the driver of the KSRTC Bus driving the vehicle on an up-gradient road, therefore Hon'ble High Court opine that, the speed of the bus must not have been high and deceased was driving the motorcycle on down gradient road could have avoided the accident by taking necessary precautions which he failed to take.
Based upon the said findings, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that, victim also responsible to the extent of 60% in causing of the accident.
But facts of the present case are totally different.
Moreover, in this case as per the above discussion, accident had occurred due to the negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
As such, non-wearing of helmet at the time of accident by the petitioner itself cannot be considered as ground to contributory negligence.
This view of this Tribunal receives the support from the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in NC:2025:KHC:39920 - DB between Smt. Lingarajamma and Naveen Kumar.

sentences.text: In view of the discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of PW.3 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata Goods Carrier bearing No. TN-70-AJ-0081.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:

The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to K.B. Sanjeevini Hospital, for first aid and later shifted to Manipal Hospital and then to St. John's Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
18. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to St. John's Medical College and Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 25.05.2024 to 18.06.2024 and again admitted to the said Hospital from 18.06.2024 to 06.07.2024 and later from 10.08.2024 to 14.08.2024 totally took treatment as inpatient for 46 days.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.17 to 19 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the St. John's Medical College and Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient for 46 days.

entities.text: St. John's Medical College and Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner also got admitted to Manipal Hospital on 25.05.2024 and discharged on the same day, the said Discharge Summary is also marked at Ex.P.24.

He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.13, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained diffuse subarachnoid hemorrhage, bilateral fronto temporo parietal subdural hematoma and also had fractures of craniofacial bones, right first rib, D1 spinous process and the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
However in support of his plea, he has produced medical bills which is marked at Ex.P.20 to the tune of Rs.11,27,898/- and also produced medical bill marked at Ex.P.24 to the tune of Rs.22,000/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,49,898/- towards medical expenses.
20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.19 Discharge summaries issued by St. John's College and Hospital, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital for about 46 days.
Hence, at least 04 month is required to recover from the accidental injuries.

It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was working as Delivery Boy at Appollo Medical Home and earning Rs.25,000/- per month, but in support of his income he has not produced any single document.

So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,500/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2024 at Rs.16,500/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench.

sentences.text: The accident is of the year is 2024.
Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- p.m. as per above decision.

21. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-
The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Shailesh A. V. Rao in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 has produced documents marked at Ex.P.5 to Ex.P.8.

He was sworn that, petitioner has sustained diffuse subarachnoid hemorrhage, bilateral fronto temporo parietal subdural hematoma and also had fractures of craniofacial bones, right first rib, D1 spinous process and he underwent tracheostomy and he has neuro disability is around 30% disability to the whole body, but he has not issued the disability certificate.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctors, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 20%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, this Tribunal consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 20%.
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Before proceeding on merits of the claim, the age of the petitioner/injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.22 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his year of birth is mentioned as 1991 and accident took place in the year 2024.
Accordingly, I assess his age as 33 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page- 3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '16'.

sentences.text: Hence petitioner is entitled for Rs.16,500 X 12 X 16 X 20% = 6,33,600/- under this head.

22. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in St. John's Medical college and Hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 25.05.2024 to 18.06.2024 and again admitted to the said Hospital from 18.06.2024 to 06.07.2024 and later from 10.08.2024 to 14.08.2024 totally took treatment as inpatient for 46 days.

23. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS :
The petitioner was aged about 33 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that, he found difficulty in doing day to day works.
He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.

Therefore,
considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.20,74,498/- under various heads.
24. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Tata Goods Carrier bearing Reg. No. TN- 70-AJ-0081 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 14.12.2024 to 13.02.2025.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 25.05.2024.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
25. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 25.05.2024.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Further the respondent No.1 denied the involvement of the offending Goods Carrier vehicle in the alleged accident and the rider of motorcycle was riding without wearing head-gear and without holding valid and effective driving license to ride the motorcycle as on the date of accident.

(i) 2009 (13) SCC 654 between Rajarani and others Vs. Oriental Insurance Co., wherein Hon'ble Apex Court observed that, contributory negligence does not mean breach of any duty.
It only means the failure by a person to use a reasonable care for the safety of either himself or his property.
Based upon the said finding Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considered the negligence on the part of deceased victim also.
